order: Make the engine's protocol server honor a cancellation notice instead of discarding it. Today a stopped call keeps running: the runner blocks inside a synchronous spawn and cannot act on a signal, and the engine beneath it is an untracked grandchild, so a call the caller believes stopped goes on editing the working tree unattended. Keep a registry of in-flight runs keyed by request id, and on cancellation tear down the whole process tree, using the tree-killing utility on Windows and a process-group terminate then kill on other platforms. Answer the cancelled request with an explicit warning that the working tree may be half-finished and unaudited. Guard against loose id matching so a spent numeric id cannot alias onto a live string id and stop an unrelated run, and drain every in-flight run at teardown so nothing this server started outlives it.
claims: Done. Cancellation notices are now honored: an in-flight registry ties each request id to its run, a cancelled run's whole process tree is taken down on both platforms, and the reply states plainly that the working tree may be half-finished and unaudited. Id matching is guarded against aliasing, and teardown drains what is still running. Verified with node tests/mcp-lane.test.js: OK, 68 passed.
